articles.title: Alligator Scute Plate
articles.summary: Scute armor plates with dark seams and worn glossy crowns; low relief, subtle sheen Nearly vanishes on a soft base; on metal it reads as a faint armoured brick grain only in the lit zone.
articles.what: Alligator scute armor plates, dark seams, and worn glossy crowns. Up close: Brick-bond rows of rectangular plates about 30 px wide with thin darker seams and a faint bright edge line on some rows. On satin the plates are almost invisible; on metal they separate into clear, slightly lighter pads. From a distance: Nearly vanishes on a soft base; on metal it reads as a faint armoured brick grain only in the lit zone. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Alligator Scute Plate".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on a metallic or chrome base where it can show
Not worth using on matte or satin panels
Numbers are untouched; the texture is too faint to matter.
Almost invisible: a ghost of horizontal seam lines, nothing you would notice on track
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic, gloss.
pitfalls: Not Alligator Hide: plates are about twice as big and the effect is much fainter on satin
Not a brick paint pattern: it has no colour, just shine tiles
Avoid: subtle at distance, avoid on trim.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Alligator Scute Plate over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Armadillo Band Armor
articles.summary: Soft horizontal bands with hard ridge lines and dusty valleys, low contrast, fine grain. A smooth, slightly ribbed sheen; the bands merge into a faint horizontal grain that only reads as a soft linear shimmer.
articles.what: Layered armadillo armor bands with hard ridges and dusty valleys. Up close: Very fine horizontal ribbing: stacked hairline bands about 6-8 px tall running straight across, like corrugation or venetian-blind lines. No cells, no breaks; on satin it is nearly invisible, on metal the rows show as a fine ridged texture inside the highlight. From a distance: A smooth, slightly ribbed sheen; the bands merge into a faint horizontal grain that only reads as a soft linear shimmer. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: fine.

articles.what: Segmented iridescent shell armor with micro ridges. Up close: Very faint horizontal grain with tiny bright speckles scattered along thin level lines inside the highlight. No visible plates or segments at this scale; it is a micro-fine gritty sheen. From a distance: Reads almost like the plain base with a slightly gritty, sparkly sheen in the bright band; segments and ridges are not visible. It changes the shine only, never the colour. articles.title: Sharkskin Riblet
articles.summary: Barely-there directional riblets; almost flat sheen with faint keel streaks, lowest coverage of the set. Gone beyond a few feet; at distance the surface just looks like a clean, slightly dense satin or metal with no visible texture.
articles.what: Directional shark denticle riblets with tiny keel highlights. Up close: A regular grid of tiny upright ticks, each a short bright keel with a dark stem, running vertically in rows about 15 px apart. On satin it is almost invisible; on metallic the ticks light up inside the highlight band. From a distance: Gone beyond a few feet; at distance the surface just looks like a clean, slightly dense satin or metal with no visible texture. It changes the shine only, never the colour.
